# Page 5^page=5
Generalised Coordinates with local basis Generalised Coordinates with local basis Recall: We are now considering generalised coordinate systems with local bases . A local basis is a basis e1, e2, e3 that varies from point to point: ej = ej(x1, x 2, x 3), e j = e j(x 1, x 2, x 3). 2 27

# Page 6^page=6
Christoffel symbols Christo˙el symbols We have a formulae relating Christo˙el symbols to the metric tensor : Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) , Γ i · jk = 1 2 giℓ ( ∂gℓj ∂xk + ∂gℓk ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xℓ ) . Recall gij = ei · ej, gij = e i · e j. Symmetry in the last two indices: The Christo˙el symbols Γi jk and Γijk are symmetric in the indices j and k. That is Γijk = Γikj, and Γi jk = Γ i kj. 3 27

# Page 7^page=7
Ricci's Theorem: Ricci's Theorem. The covariant derivative of the metric tensor gik vanishes. Useful formula Ricci's theorem yields the following useful formula ∂gik ∂xℓ = Γikℓ + Γkiℓ. In particular, in orthogonal coordinates Γikℓ + Γkiℓ = 0 =⇒ Γikℓ = −Γkiℓ. 4 27

# Page 8^page=8
RiemannChristoffel tensor RiemannChristo˙el To check whether we are in Euclidean space , we check whether the space has zero curvature. That is, whether covariant derivatives commute: ∇j∇kAi = ∇k∇jAi. We de˝ne the RiemannChristo˙el tensor by Rr ijkAr = ∇j∇kAi − ∇k∇jAi. We have shown Rr ijk = ∂Γr ki ∂xj − ∂Γr ij ∂xk + Γp ikΓ r pj − Γ p ijΓ r pk. 5 27

# Page 9^page=9
RiemannChristoffel tensor properties RiemannChristo˙el tensor properties Rr ijk is a tensor. A space is Euclidean if and only if the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor vanishes. 6 27

# Page 11^page=11
Ricci tensor De˝nition. The Ricci tensor is de˝ned as a trace of the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor, that is Rij = Rk ikj. Riemann-Christo˙el tensor and the Christo˙el symbols In terms of the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor and the Christo˙el symbols, one has Rij = Rk ikj = ∂ ∂xk Γ k ji − ∂ ∂xj Γ k ik + Γp ijΓ k pk − Γ p ikΓk pj This is a symmetric tensor. 7 27

# Page 12^page=12
Goal In the next slides, we will solve the following. Question In this question, consider the three-dimensional coordinate system (x1, x2, x3) = (ρ, θ, z) with position r given by r = ρ cos θi1 + ρ sin θi2 + zi3, where i1, i2, i3 are the usual Cartesian basis vectors. Find the Ricci tensor with respect to this coordinate system. 8 27

# Page 13^page=13
Revision Revision This exercise will revise many concepts of the previous weeks. The Ricci tensor is a trace of the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor, that is Rij = Rk ikj. Thus, we need to compute the components of the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor Rrijk. In turn, to ˝nd the components of the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor, we need the Christo˙el symbols Γi jk. The Christo˙el symbols depend on the metric coe˚cients gij and gij. To ˝nd the metic coe˚cients, we need the basis vectors e1, e2, e3. 9 27

# Page 14^page=14
Basis vectors Basis vectors To ˝nd the basis vectors e1, e2, e3 of the given coordinate system, we use the formula ei = ∂r ∂xi . Again, we are taking the coordinate system (x1, x2, x3) = (ρ, θ, z) with position r given by r = ρ cos θi1 + ρ sin θi2 + zi3. Thus e1 = ∂r ∂x1 = ∂r ∂ρ = cos θi1 + sin θi2, e2 = ∂r ∂x2 = ∂r ∂θ = −ρ sin θi1 + ρ cos θi2, e3 = ∂r ∂x3 = ∂r ∂z = i3. 10 27

# Page 15^page=15
Metric coefficients Metric coe˚cients Let us compute the metric tensor components gij. Let us start with the ones where i ̸= j. g12 = e1 · e2 =   cos θ sin θ 0   ·  −ρ sin θ ρ cos θ 0   = −ρ cos θ sin θ + ϕ cos θ sin θ = 0, g13 = e1 · e3 =   cos θ sin θ 0   ·  0 0 1   = 0, g23 = e2 · e3 =   −ρ sin θ ρ cos θ 0   ·  0 0 1   = 0. Since gij = gji, this shows that gij = 0 whenever i ̸= j. 11 27

# Page 16^page=16
Orthogonality Orthogonality A coordinate system with basis e1, e2, e3 is orthogonal whenever ei · ej = 0 if i ̸= j. We have showen that ei · ej = 0 whenever i ̸= j, so we conclude that this coordinate system is orthogonal . Note that ei · ej = 0 whenever i ̸= j is equivalent to gij = 0 for i ̸= j. 12 27

# Page 17^page=17
Metric coefficients - part 2 Metric coe˚cients - part 2 Let us now compute the metric tensor components of the form gii. g11 = e1 · e1 =   cos θ sin θ 0   ·  cos θ sin θ 0   = cos 2 θ + sin2 θ = 1, g22 = e2 · e2 = ( −ρ sin θ ρ cos θ ) · ( −ρ sin θ ρ cos θ ) = ρ 2 sin 2 θ + ρ 2 cos2 θ = ρ 2(sin 2 θ + cos2 θ) = ρ 2, g33 = e3 · e3 =   0 0 1   ·  0 0 1   = 1. 13 27

# Page 18^page=18
Orthonormality Orthonormality A coordinate system with basis e1, e2, e3 is orthonormal whenever ei · ej = δij. Equivalently whenever gij = δij. We showed that gij = ei · ej = 0 whenever i ̸= j. g11 = e1 · e1 = 1 and g33 = e3 · e3 = 1. However, g22 = e2 · e2 = ρ2 ̸= 1. Thus, this system is not orthonormal. 14 27

# Page 19^page=19
Arc length (Extra!) Arc length Let us also describe the arc length element in terms of the metric coe˚cients. 1 Since the system is orthogonal and [gij] = ( 1 0 0 0 ρ2 0 0 0 1 ) , the arc length element is given by (ds) 2 = g11dx1dx1 + g22dx2dx2 + g33dx 3dx3 = (dρ) 2 + (ρdθ)2 + (dz) 2. Thus, the metric coe˚cients are h1 = 1, h2 = ρ, h3 = 1. 1 Note this is not needed to reach our goal! 15 27

# Page 20^page=20
Christoffel symbols of first kind Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind Let us ˝nd all Christo˙el symbols Γijk of the ˝rst kind for the given coordinate system. Recall Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . Since [gij] = ( 1 0 0 0 ρ2 0 0 0 1 ) , we see that the only non-zero ∂gmn ∂xp is ∂g22 ∂x1 = ∂ρ2 ∂ρ = 2ρ. Thus then only non-zero Γijk are the ones with two indices 2 and one index 1. That is, Γ122, Γ212, and Γ221. 16 27

# Page 21^page=21
Christoffel symbols Γijk- Part 2 Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind Again, the only non-zero ∂gmn ∂xp is ∂g22 ∂x1 = ∂ρ2 ∂ρ = 2ρ. That is, Γ122, Γ212 = Γ221 are the only non-zero Γijk. Now Γ122 = 1 2 ( ∂g12 ∂x2 + ∂g12 ∂x2 − ∂g22 ∂x1 ) = − 1 2 ∂g22 ∂ρ = − 1 2 (2ρ) = −ρ. By Ricci's Theorem, Γ212 = −Γ122 = ρ. By the symmetry of Christo˙el symbols on the last two indices, we also have Γ221 = Γ212 = ρ. 17 27

# Page 22^page=22
Christoffel symbols Γijk- Conclusion Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind - Conclusion We conclude Γ122 = −ρ, Γ212 = ρ, Γ221 = ρ, Γijk = 0, for all other values of i, j, k. 18 27

# Page 23^page=23
Christoffel symbols of second kind Christo˙el symbols of second kind Let us ˝nd the Christo˙el symbols of second kind. We have [gij] = ( 1 0 0 0 ρ2 0 0 0 1 ) so [gij] = ( 1 0 0 0 1 ρ2 0 0 0 1 ) . Therefore Γ 1 22 = g1ℓΓℓ22 = g11Γ122 = 1 · (−ρ) = −ρ, Γ 2 21 = Γ 2 12 = g2 21Γ221 = 1 ρ2 ρ = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for all other values of i, j, k. 19 27

# Page 24^page=24
Riemann-Christoffel tensor Riemann-Christo˙el tensor To illustrate how to compute the components of the Riemann-Christo˙el tensor, let us ˝nd R2 121. We found Γ 1 22 = −ρ, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for other i, j, k. Thus, R2 121 = ∂ ∂x2 Γ 2 11 − ∂ ∂x1 Γ2 12 + Γp 11Γ 2 p2 − Γ p 12Γ 2 p1 = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 2 12 + Γp 11Γ2 p2 − Γ p 12Γ 2 p1 (Γ 2 11 = 0). 20 27

# Page 25^page=25
Riemann-Christoffel tensor Riemann-Christo˙el tensor Again Γ 1 22 = −ρ, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for other i, j, k. Continuing R2 121 = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 2 12 + Γp 11Γ2 p2 − Γ p 12Γ 2 p1 = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 2 12 + ( ˆ ˆΓ1 11Γ 2 12 + ˆ ˆΓ 2 11ˆˆˆΓ2 22 + ˆ ˆΓ 3 11ˆˆˆΓ 2 32) − Γ p 12Γ 2 p1 = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 2 12 − ˆˆˆΓ1 12ˆ ˆˆΓ 2 11 − Γ 2 12Γ 2 21 − ˆ ˆˆΓ 3 12ˆˆˆΓ 2 31 = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 2 12 − Γ2 12Γ 2 21 = − ∂ ∂ρ ( 1 ρ ) − 1 ρ · 1 ρ = 1 ρ2 − 1 ρ2 = 0. 21 27

# Page 26^page=26
Ricci tensor Ricci tensor Let us ˝nd the Ricci tensor Rij = Rk ikj = R1 i1j + R2 i2j. Let us ˝nd all values of R1 i1j and of R2 i2j separately. 22 27

# Page 27^page=27
Ricci tensor - R1 i1j Γ 1 22 = −ρ, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for other i, j, k. Ricci tensor R1 i1j First, we have R1 i1j = ∂ ∂xj ˆ ˆΓ 1 1i − ∂ ∂x1 Γ1 ij + Γp i1Γ 1 pj − Γ p ijˆˆˆΓ1 p1 = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 1 ij + Γp i1Γ1 pj = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 1 ij + ˆ ˆΓ1 i1ˆˆˆΓ1 1j + Γ2 i1Γ 1 2j = − ∂ ∂x1 Γ 1 ij + Γ2 i1Γ1 2j = { 0, if i = 1 or j = 1 1 + 1 ρ (−ρ) = 0, otherwise . 23 27

# Page 28^page=28
Ricci tensor - R2 i2j - case 1 Γ 1 22 = −ρ, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for other i, j, k. Ricci tensor R2 i2j - case 1 Moreover R2 i2j = ∂ ∂xj Γ 2 2i − ∂ ∂x2 Γ 2 ij ︸ ︷︷ ︸ ∂ ∂x2 (Γi jk)=0 +Γ p i2Γ 2 pj − Γ p ijΓ 2 p2 = ∂ ∂xj Γ 2 2i + Γp i2Γ2 pj − Γp ijΓ 2 p2. If (i, j) = (1, 2) or (i, j) = (2, 1), then R2 i2j = ∂ ∂xj Γ 2 2i ︸ ︷︷ ︸ =0 +Γ p i2Γ 2 pj − Γ p ijΓ2 p2 = Γ 1 i2Γ 2 1j ︸ ︷︷ ︸ =0 + Γ 2 i2Γ2 2j ︸ ︷︷ ︸ =0 − � �Γ 1 ijΓ 2 12 − Γ 2 ijˆ ˆˆΓ 2 22 = 0. 24 27

# Page 29^page=29
Ricci tensor - R2 i2j - case 2 Γ 1 22 = −ρ, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for other i, j, k. Ricci tensor R2 i2j - case 2 In the previous slide, we have shown R2 122 = 0, R2 221 = 0, In a previous slide we already computed R2 121 = 0. Thus to ˝nish all R2 i2j, we need to compute R2 222. 25 27

# Page 30^page=30
Ricci tensor - R2 222 Γ 1 22 = −ρ, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 ρ , Γ i jk = 0, for other i, j, k. Ricci tensor R2 222 Finally, since R2 i2j = ∂ ∂xj Γ 2 2i + Γp i2Γ 2 pj − Γ p ijΓ 2 p2, we get R2 222 = ∂ ∂x2ˆˆˆΓ 2 22 + Γp 22Γ2 p2 − Γ p 22Γ 2 p2 Γ 1 22Γ 2 12 + ˆ ˆΓ 2 22ˆˆˆΓ 2 22 − Γ1 22Γ 2 12 − ˆˆˆΓ 2 22ˆˆˆΓ 2 22 = 0. 26 27

# Page 31^page=31
Ricci tensor - Conclusion Ricci tensor - Conclusion We have found that for all i, j ∈ {1, 2} R1 i1j = 0, R2 i2j = 0. Therefore, Rij = Rk ikj = R1 i1j + R2 i2j = 0, for all i, j. 27 / 27
